still_unresolved: Whether prioritizing closed storage receptacles over open surfaces yields faster target acquisition for objects typically stored inside enclosed containers.
Whether the general listed-order search strategy should be refined to incorporate object-type heuristics for initial receptacle selection.

updates.evidence_basis: Probe navigated to and opened cabinet_1 first per hypothesis guidance, found no soapbar, then successfully acquired soapbar_1 from countertop_1. Target was on an open surface, not in a closed receptacle, costing 2 additional actions (go to + open) before finding it.
updates.guidance: When searching for a target object not visible at room center, recognize that some object types (e.g., soapbar) may frequently appear on open surfaces like countertops even when closed storage receptacles are available. Blindly prioritizing closed receptacles first can incur unnecessary navigation and opening costs if the target is actually on an open surface. Consider inspecting open surfaces early in the search order, or use object-type priors to decide whether to check closed or open receptacles first.
updates.scope: ALFWorld pick-clean-then-place tasks where the target object type is known but not visible at room center, and both closed storage receptacles and open surfaces are available in the admissible action list.
